name: Customer Obsession
definition: Leaders start with the customer and work backwards. They work hard to earn and keep customer trust. They watch competitors. They obsess over customers.

rows.under: Optimizes for internal convenience. Does not put the customer experience first.
rows.justRight: Starts with the customer and works backwards. Seeks feedback and uses it to improve.
rows.over: Makes too many exceptions to a sound process because one customer asked.

rows.under: Asks customers too late, or not at all, when building something new.
rows.justRight: Looks for feedback on a cadence. Builds service metrics. Seeks input before the plan is frozen.
rows.over: Changes the plan with every single comment. Loses the greater customer good.

rows.under: The wrong work gets done. No customer feels heard. The people doing the work are on a death march.
rows.justRight: Customers understand the vision. Even when their request is not first, they can see why the current work is best for the collective good. You listen, then push back so the long-term right thing ships.
rows.over: Promises too much to keep every customer happy. Cannot rank requests. Deadlines slip and the team burns out from churn.

rows.situation: A customer complains about a product they bought
rows.under: Ignores the complaint because it is only one customer.
rows.justRight: Investigates, and confirms the product is described accurately and is not defective. Fixes it if it is faulty, and replaces it when that is the honest fix. Tells the customer what you found.
rows.over: Pulls the entire listing because one person complained.

rows.under: Ignores it if the amount is small.
rows.justRight: Refunds the exact overcharge without being asked. If you caused extra fees (an overdraft, a penalty), you cover those too.
rows.over: Sends a gift certificate well above the error and calls that the process.

rows.under: Feedback arrives only through escalations. It is not part of weekly measurement.
rows.justRight: Customer need is a regular part of the week. You know whether they had a good week, and whether the work ahead will help them in a significant way.
rows.over: Treats every comment as an urgent daily priority. Rewrites the plan weekly for feedback that is not researched or understood.

rows.under: Builds it and hopes they will come. Falls in love with the technology.
rows.justRight: Works backwards from the end-user need. Delivers value in increments. Rechecks whether the product is meeting the need.
rows.over: Tries to build the perfect product that meets every demand at once.
